packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

PACKET-03 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (low confidence throughout)

Exposure statement
No proposed identification of work or author, and no earlier reading, reached me in my context. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..020.jpg (plus the filtered filename listing described in packet-01.txt). Nothing else beyond the rules.

Layout survey (observation)
- image-001: overview of one face (I call it face 1) of a paper or thin parchment bifolium-shaped sheet lying landscape, about 28 x 19.5 cm by the ruler, with a vertical central fold. It looks like a sheet recovered from a binding: the surface is covered with brown paste/leather residue, there are wormholes and losses, and the ink is washed to a pale grey-brown.
- image-014: overview of the other face (face 2), darker and more heavily encrusted.
- image-002..013: native tiles of face 1 in a 4-wide by 3-high grid read in this order: 002 (top, right of fold, left part), 003 (top right), 004 (middle, right of fold), 005 (middle right), 006 (bottom, right of fold), 007 (bottom right), 008 (top left), 009 (top, left of fold), 010 (middle left), 011 (middle, left of fold), 012 (bottom left), 013 (bottom, left of fold). Neighbouring tiles overlap by several lines.
- image-015..020: native tiles of the right half of face 2 only: 015 (top, right of fold), 016 (top right), 017 (middle), 018 (middle right), 019 (bottom), 020 (bottom right). The left half of face 2 has no tiles; in the overview it shows no legible writing, only residue (a small red mark at the top-left edge).
- Face 1, right half: one block of about 33 long lines in a small, rapid, strongly abbreviated cursive bookhand. Red is used for paraph-like strokes inside lines, for two L-shaped brackets (one at the left of a line about a third of the way down, one framing the last word of the block), for a red strike-through of one word, and for a marginal sign at the right edge. No enlarged initial, no running title seen on this half.
- Face 1, left half: about 12 lines at the top only, fainter and greyer, with a short note in the top margin above them and small marginal numerals at the left edge that I read as "p°", "2°", "3°" (and a fourth mark lower). Below these lines the left half is blank or lost under residue; at the very foot, left, one word in larger pale script.
- Face 2, right half: about 23 lines in the same or a similar cursive, with red paraph strokes and a square bracket-like sign at the left margin about line 10; a paragraph break (short last line) about line 23; then, after a gap, five lines in a different, larger, looser and paler cursive with big looped ascenders (a later addition or a note in another hand: tentative interpretation).
- Tentative interpretation: the two halves are two pages of a folded sheet (a bifolium), each with a single column, so the text on the left half and right half of one face need not be continuous. I cannot determine page order.

Areas selected / unread
- I worked hardest on the three most legible areas: face 1 right half upper part (image-003, image-005), face 2 right half upper and middle (image-016, image-017, image-018), and the foot of face 2 (image-019, image-020).
- Not read: the left-hand beginnings of most lines of the face 1 right block (image-002, image-004: washed to smudges), the lower third of that block (image-006, image-007: only isolated words), the face 1 left block (image-008, image-009: isolated words), and face 2 line beginnings in image-015.
- This script is at the limit of what I can read from these images. Many words below are shape-readings, marked with "?". Where I could not get even a shape-reading I wrote [illegible] and did not fill from sense.

Conventions
- "]" = text continues to the left out of the tile or is unread there. Abbreviation marks I could see are kept as raised strokes or described; proposed expansions are in parentheses. "7" = the Tironian et. "ɔ" = the con-sign. "|" = a red or ink paraph stroke inside the line.

Summary of what I would actually rely on
- Structure: marginal numerals p° / 2° / 3° beside the face 1 left block; rubricated brackets and paraphs; a red-struck deletion (image-005 l.4); a red-bracketed final word at the foot of the face 1 right block; a later five-line addition at the foot of face 2.
- Words with moderate confidence: "nemo ambigit" (image-003 l.9), "ab eo" (l.11), "celebrare" and "de clericis" (image-005 l.5-6), "postulaba-" (image-016 l.9), "rebelles" (image-017 l.9), "filio" (image-008 l.3). Everything else carries a question mark for a reason.

Limitations
- The ink is washed out and overlaid by residue; the hand is a fast, heavily abbreviated cursive in which minims, c/t, and the many suspension strokes are not separable at this state of preservation. I may have misdivided words and misread abbreviations wholesale.
- Line numbers are counted per tile and the top line of several tiles is a partial line; treat them as approximate to plus or minus one.
- Line beginnings of the face 1 right block and all of the face 2 left half are effectively unread.
- Column and page order is unknown.
- Helpful next images: UV or infrared of both faces (the ink is likely to respond); tiles for the left half of face 2; a contrast-stretched single-channel (blue) rendering of image-002, -004, -006 and -015.
